changes: Lowered scribe confidence from high to medium: 'likhitaṃ śivaḥ śubhaṃ' most likely names the scribe Śiva, but it could also be an auspicious formula (śivaḥ/śubham).
Gave month as the solar month Siṃha (from 'pañcānanagate ravau'); added this to notes.
Reworded notes: the catalogue's 'SAM 1728' is the right number, but the era label is misleading. The colophon says Śaka explicitly.

date.as_written: śakeṣṭa dvinagābjābde paṃcānanagete ravau | sitedale daśabhyāṃ sūryaje

notes: The chronogram aṣṭa (8), dvi (2), naga (7), abja (1), read right to left, gives Śaka 1728, about 1806 CE. 'pañcānanagate ravau' means the sun was in Siṃha (Leo), so the date falls in the solar month Siṃha, roughly Bhādrapada. 'sitadale daśamyāṃ sūryaje' means śukla 10, a Saturday. The colophon names the Śaka era explicitly. The catalogue's 'SAM 1728' has the right number but should not be read as Vikrama Saṃvat. 'likhitaṃ śivaḥ' is taken as the scribe's name, but it may be part of a closing auspicious formula.
